disconfirming_evidence: Bitquery explicitly says the bot funding/collector pattern fits one Binance customer rather than Binance itself; no operator identity is established.
The exact rDAE53 address match does not connect the bot operator to the theft actor; exchange omnibus wallets can service unrelated customers.
The bot cluster shut down on 14–16 October, while the XRP incident transfer occurred on 29 October.
The post-incident transfers to rs8Z are public ledger payments between Bithomp-labelled Binance accounts, not proof of official reserve replenishment or recovery.
Bithomp account title and body balance fields disagree; no raw account_info or independent second explorer balance was obtained.
The $7.33B RLUSD figure is gross ledger transfer value, not net capital; issuer plumbing and a matched roundtrip account for about 31.65% of it.
Cross River announcement timing does not establish why the bot cluster shut down; Bitquery found no ledger explanation.
Bitquery is one analytics provider; media republication of its article would not be independent on-chain corroboration.
No attacker-receiver refresh later than the previously captured 06:43 UTC observation was obtained.
